'''Seswenna''' was an [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] located in the [[Seswenna sector/Legends|Seswenna sector]]. By [[3699 BBY]], Seswenna lay on what would eventually become the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]] [[Super-hyperroute/Legends|super-hyperroute]]. However, the Hydian Way had shifted by [[1004 BBY]] to go through the [[Eriadu system/Legends|Eriadu system]] instead. During the late period of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] rule, Seswenna served as the [[Sector/Legends|sector]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]], but that status would similarly pass to the planet [[Eriadu/Legends|Eriadu]] over [[Time/Legends|time]].

The future [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Admiral/Legends|admiral]] [[Conan Antonio Motti/Legends|Conan Antonio Motti]] was [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] on Seswenna. By the time the Empire reigned, the planet temporarily housed the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] project as well as [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]] [[Shipyard/Legends|shipyards]].

==Description==
Seswenna was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="DeathStarCoup">{{InsiderCite|Special Edition 2014|A Certain Point of View|A Certain Point of View: The Death Star Coup}}</ref> located in the [[Seswenna system/Legends|Seswenna system]]. It was a part of the [[Seswenna sector/Legends|Seswenna sector]],<ref name="EAOC" /> within the [[Trailing Sectors/Legends|Trailing Sectors]] portion of<ref name="TEA" /> the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="EAOC" />

==History==
===Under the Republic===
As part of the [[Seswenna Expansion]] between [[3701 BBY]] and [[3699 BBY]], a new [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] was [[Scout/Legends|charted]]. It extended from the [[Malastare system/Legends|Malastare system]] in the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] and ran through the [[Grumani sector/Legends|Grumani sector's]] [[Knel'char system|Darkknell system]] and Seswenna before terminating at the [[Colu system|Clak'dor system]], in the [[Mayagil sector/Legends|Mayagil sector]].<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:Eriadu.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The planet Eriadu eventually overshadowed its neighbor Seswenna.]]
The route would eventually be integrated into a [[Super-hyperroute/Legends|super-hyperroute]] known as the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]].<ref name="TEA" /> However, over [[Time/Legends|time]], many [[Merchant/Legends|traders]] traveling down the Hydian Way chose to deviate from the route in favor of the loop known as the [[Eriadu Way|Eriadu Bypass]],<ref name="GATORW" /> and by [[1004 BBY]], the Hydian had shifted to run through the neighboring [[Eriadu system/Legends|Eriadu system]] instead of Seswenna.<ref name="TEA" />

Seswenna served as the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] world of the Seswenna [[Sector/Legends|sector]] during the last [[Standard century/Legends|century]] of the existence of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. By that time, a movement was growing inside the sector that called for the acknowledgment of economic reality and transferring the status of capital to the planet [[Eriadu/Legends|Eriadu]]. Indeed, Eriadu would eventually become the administrative center of the sector upon the ascension of the Republic [[Governor/Legends|Governor]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]] to the [[Military rank/Legends|rank]] of [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] within the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="GATORW" />

===Rise of the Empire===
[[File:DS1_under_construction.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Seswenna temporarily housed the headquarters of the Death Star superweapon project.]]
[[Standard year/Legends|Years]] before the conflict known as the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] took place, the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Conan Antonio Motti/Legends|Conan Antonio Motti]] was [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] on Seswenna. Motti would eventually go on to serve as an [[Admiral/Legends|admiral]] with the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]].<ref name="AuthorsCut">{{SW|url=news/the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-part-11-serving-the-empire|series=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|text=Part 11: Serving the Empire}}</ref> Following the [[Mission to Mustafar/Legends|end]] of the Clone Wars in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], Seswenna temporarily became the headquarters for the Imperial project developing the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] after it was moved from the [[Arkanis sector/Legends|Arkanis sector]] planet [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]]. The project was eventually relocated again to the [[Patriim system/Legends|Patriim system]].<ref name="TEA" />

During the reign of the Empire, Seswenna shared its name with the [[Carrack-class light cruiser/Legends|''Carrack''-class light cruiser]] ''[[Seswennan Nightcloak]]''.<ref name="Planets3">''[[Planets of the Galaxy, Volume Three]]''</ref> The planet was [[Orbit/Legends|orbited]] by [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]] [[Shipyard/Legends|shipyards]] by the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], fought between the Empire and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]]. At some point before the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], a [[Special Ops Team]] of [[Alliance Special Operations/Legends|Alliance Special Operations]] exploited a weakness in the security network of the shipyards in order to wreak havoc upon the Imperial military operations.<ref name="GG9" />

==Behind the scenes==
Seswenna was first mentioned in ''[[Galaxy Guide 9: Fragments from the Rim]]'', a [[1993]] sourcebook written by [[Simon Smith]] and [[Eric S. Trautmann]] for [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''.<ref name="GG9" /> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed the Seswenna [[Star system/Legends|system]], and therefore the planet Seswenna, in grid square M-18.<ref name="TEA" />
